summary: H.R. 3168, the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2025, extends federal earthquake hazard reduction activities through fiscal year 2030. The bill directs federal agencies, particularly the U.S. Geological Survey, to expand earthquake early warning systems into new high-risk areas, improve alert broadcasting in coordination with the Federal Communications Commission, issue aftershock forecasts, and incorporate tsunamis and other secondary hazards into seismic mapping and building codes.

affected_groups.effect: Must coordinate data sharing, resource allocation, emergency alert broadcasting, and hazard reduction activities.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (USGS, FEMA, NIST, NSF, NOAA, FCC)

affected_groups.effect: Included explicitly in program planning, hazard mitigation, and earthquake early warning system improvements.
Benefit from expanded early warning systems, multi-language alerts broadcast more rapidly, aftershock forecasts, and improved post-earthquake recovery planning for community infrastructure.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes funding for the U.S. Geological Survey under the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program at $83,403,000 annually from fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2030, with at least $30,000,000 each year designated for completing the Advanced National Seismic System.

Requires the U.S. Geological Survey to coordinate with the Federal Communications Commission to ensure earthquake alerts and early warnings are broadcast as rapidly and reliably as possible in the predominant languages of affected regions.
Expands the earthquake early warning system into additional high-risk hazard areas and directs the issuance of forecasts for aftershocks following significant earthquakes.
Directs the inclusion of tsunamis, tsunami susceptibility, and other natural hazards associated with earthquakes into seismic hazard maps and program activities.

Updates building codes, standards, and guidelines to include post-earthquake recovery-based performance objectives addressing the reoccupancy and downtime of community-prioritized buildings and infrastructure.
Includes Tribal governments alongside state and local governments in program activities, hazard mitigation planning, and advisory committees.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact current baseline budget or how funding amounts compare to previous authorization levels beyond what is listed for FY2026-FY2030.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 3168, the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2025, extends federal earthquake hazard reduction activities through fiscal year 2030. The bill directs federal agencies, particularly the U.S. Geological Survey, to expand earthquake early warning systems into new high-risk areas, improve alert broadcasting in coordination with the Federal Communications Commission, issue aftershock forecasts, and incorporate tsunamis and other secondary hazards into seismic mapping and building codes.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides ongoing funding authority of over $83 million per year through 2030 for federal earthquake monitoring, mapping, and warning infrastructure. Its significance lies in modernizing emergency alerts, expanding geographic coverage for early warnings, integrating secondary threats like tsunamis into hazard preparation, and focusing building standards on post-disaster recovery and building functionality.
